items.response:
A cardboard fort is a good pick, and Leo already has fort experience from the one he built out of the reno boxes in May, door and 'no grownups' sign included. For tomorrow you will mostly want strong tape (duct or packing), a box cutter or sturdy scissors for you to do the cutting, markers for windows and signs, and some blankets or clips to drape over the top. A flashlight or string lights make it feel like a real hideout.
Action: I'd turn that into a short supply list so you can check what's in the basement tonight, and flag whatever you need to pick up before school ends tomorrow.

Pulling your personal notes from this month now, and I'll just show them to you when they're in, no running commentary.
Action: Fetch this month's personal notes and show them as a simple list with title and last-edited date, so you can start tidying.

I don't want to guess at the weather for that day, so I'd rather look it up than give you something that sounds right. I'll check what Ottawa actually recorded on the 25th (high, low, snow, wind chill) so you can settle it with Grace.
Action: Look up Ottawa's observed weather for the 25th and report temperatures, snowfall and wind chill.

Glad you landed safe. I don't have the earlier flight search or the Lafourcade song piece in front of me, so I'd go find both rather than reconstruct them from memory.
Action: Search our earlier conversations for the flight search from before you booked and for the Lafourcade song write-up, then send you the fare comparison for Kabir and the song piece for Mei. If I can't find either, I'll tell you and re-run it.

3:30pm for 25 minutes ends at 3:55, which is inside your 9:30 to 16:30 window, but your rule is nothing after 15:00 on Fridays, so I need to check what day the 9th falls on. I also need to check Olivia's and Aisha's calendars for that slot.
Action: If the 9th isn't a Friday and all three of you are free, I'll book 15:30 to 15:55 with your three agenda items (where certification stands, what sales can and can't say, next checkpoint). If it is a Friday, I'll propose a slot before 15:00 instead.

I don't have Sam's text in front of me, so I'll open it and see what he's asking before suggesting anything. Then I'll work out a dinner for tonight that doesn't depend on the hotplate.
Action: Read Sam's text about dinner, then come back with two or three no-hotplate options (takeout nearby or something simple that needs no cooking) that fit whatever he said.

That sounds lovely, enjoy the coffee and the sun. I'll park the career day talk until you want it, and your prep block is already on the calendar for Tue 31 Mar, so there's no rush.
Action: Nothing for now. I'll leave the talk draft alone until you ask.

An EFT is a batch electronic transfer that goes through the clearing system: it's cheap, usually takes one to a few business days to settle, and can be returned or reversed. A wire is a one-off, high-value payment that moves quickly, is generally final once sent, and costs more, so it's used for large or urgent amounts. For merchant payouts, EFT is the normal rail and a wire is the exception, which is why using them interchangeably in decks is misleading.
Action: I can draft a two-line definition you can drop into sales' deck comments so the wording gets fixed in one pass.

Let's get someone out for the outside tap today or Monday. In the meantime, if there's an inside shut-off for that tap (usually in the basement), turning it off will stop the drip and the hose problem until the plumber arrives.
Action: Search for well-reviewed plumbers near Leslieville who can come today or Monday, check their earliest openings, and send you three options with reviews and availability to pick from.

Happy to set this up, but I don't have your class time or what you covered last lesson in front of me. I'd check the calendar for the class and look at your latest lesson notes so the focus areas are based on what you actually need.
Action: Find the class on your calendar, check what the last session covered, then block two study sessions before the class on days you're free and send you a short list of focus areas.

Adding it now: Toronto Waterfront Half Marathon, October 19, 2025, 2:04:37. That works out to roughly 5:54 per km over 21.1 km. I'll mark it as the official result so the December recap uses it.
Action: Add the race to your running stats as an official result and tag it for the yearly recap.

I'll pull Tom's calendar for the 24th and show you when he was actually open, along with what filled the rest of the day, which is the useful part for your write-up. Since it's March now, I'll assume you mean the 24th of last month, and I'll confirm that on the calendar.
Action: Pull Tom's calendar for the 24th, list his free slots and the blocks that covered the rest of the day, and send it to you.

Anytime. Tom's request for the beta merchant numbers link is still open for after dinner, and your two ready holds are waiting at Pape/Danforth until Sat 25 Apr.
Action: Nothing more for now.

Noted: Jess from Rover walks him at noon on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at $25 a walk, which comes to $75 a week. Starting Monday also means starting on cabinet delivery day (Mon 10 Nov, 8 to 10am, with Nate there from 7:30), so Jess will need a way in.
Action: Add a recurring Mon/Wed/Fri 12:00 'Biscuit walk (Jess, Rover)' event from Monday, add a $75 per week line to the pet budget, and ask how Jess will get in on Monday.

I'll reorder the Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach in salmon, and I'll check the listing carefully before ordering so it isn't a chicken-based flavour. If the title and ingredients don't clearly show salmon, I'll hold the order and tell you instead of guessing.
Action: Find the salmon Sensitive Skin & Stomach listing in the same size as last time, verify flavour and ingredients, and place the order if it matches.

Both are on my list. I don't know the Pape branch's Saturday hours, so I'll check them before setting the pickup time, since the closing time I have is for weekdays.
Action: Set a reminder Friday morning to send Tom your strategy memo comments, check Pape/Danforth's Saturday hours, then set a Saturday morning reminder for the library books pickup within them.

Here's a tighter version: 'If a payout fails because of a bank-side error, the system automatically retries it without any action from the merchant.' It drops the passive phrasing and keeps the requirement testable.
Action: Swap it into the PRD at that requirement once you're happy with it.

Happy to look. For the August long weekend (Civic Holiday is Mon 3 Aug), I'll price Air Canada first since that's your preference with Aeroplan, standard economy or better rather than basic, aisle seats, shown in CAD. I'll price it for just you and for you plus Leo so you can compare.
Action: Search Air Canada Toronto to Vancouver around Fri 31 Jul to Mon 3 Aug, non-basic fares, and report a rough CAD range for one and for two travellers.

Timer set for 25 minutes. Enjoy the garden beds.
Action: Start a 25-minute timer now and alert you when it goes off.

I'll look for a late-morning opening with Dr. Lin on Apr 22 and check it against your calendar first. If there's no slot that day, I'll find the closest late-morning alternatives.
Action: Check your calendar for the morning of Apr 22, check Dr. Lin's office for a late-morning cleaning, book it if available, and otherwise send you the nearest options.

Saved to a private health note: penicillin allergy (hives), and seasonal allergies in May managed with Reactine.
Action: Create a private health note with those two items, and tell you where it lives.

Okay, the charcoal bag order stays on hold until you've checked with Sam. East End Plumbing is confirmed for Mon 29 Jun, 09:00 to 12:00 with Raj, and they need the inside shut-off valve to be accessible.
Action: Hold the order and wait for your word.

The commute gap is bigger than it looks: 10 minutes by bike versus 45 on the subway is about 70 minutes a day, roughly 6 hours a week. I'd tell him to turn the 10% into after-tax dollars per month and compare it to those hours, then weigh caseload, mentorship and growth path, since those usually matter more than either number. Unless the pay gap is large in real dollars, the shorter commute is hard to beat.
Action: If you send me his rough salary, I'll work out what the extra 10% is worth per commute hour so you can give him a number.

I'd rather read your actual calendars than guess, so let me pull next week's from both your work and family calendars.
Action: Pull next week's events from your work and family calendars and send you a day-by-day rundown with any conflicts flagged.

Booking East End Plumbing for Monday morning, 29 Jun. For the Lattice self-review due Fri 10 Jul, I'll remind you to start next week on Tuesday 30 Jun so it doesn't collide with the plumber on Monday morning, then again the week of the deadline.
Action: Book East End Plumbing for Mon 29 Jun, and set Lattice reminders for Tue 30 Jun (start) and Mon 6 Jul (due Friday).

I don't have that saved in front of me, so I'd rather find what you actually said than guess how you learn best. Once I have it, I'll tie the vocab to it for tonight.
Action: Search your notes and our past chats for how you said you learn Spanish best and any vocab preferences, then send them back with a short plan for tonight's practice.

Here's a draft: 'Hey Hannah, Leo and I are heading to Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30 for the playground and the market. Want to come with the kids? No pressure if you've got other plans.'
Action: Hold it for your OK, then send it to Hannah.

I'll ask Olivia whether QBR prep can move to 11:00 so it stops clashing with your Q1 roadmap check-in. For Ellie, I don't have a pantry inventory, so I can't say what's in the house, and dairy hides in crackers, granola bars and some cookies, so the labels matter.
Action: Message Olivia asking for 11:00, and check recent grocery orders for dairy-free snacks that you have, then send you a list with any that need a label check.

¡Claro! Quiz rápido de excepciones, una pregunta a la vez. Primera: ¿se dice 'el mano' o 'la mano'?
Action: Esperar tu respuesta, corregirla en una línea y seguir con 'mapa' y 'problema' hasta que se acaben tus 10 minutos.

Tripling it is easy: multiply every ingredient by three, including the chips and vanilla, and keep the bake time and temperature the same, just use more trays and bake in batches. I don't have the one-dozen quantities from December in front of me, so I'd rather find them than guess.
Action: Find our 2025-12-13 chat for the one-dozen amounts and send you the tripled list. If I can't find it, I'll ask you to read me the quantities off the bag.

On it, short version coming.
Action: Find this afternoon's all-hands email and send you the 4 things that matter as four short bullets.

The May long weekend is Victoria Day weekend, and Ottawa's tulip festival usually runs around then, which is a good one with Leo. I don't have what you looked into last spring, so I'll search for it and confirm the dates rather than trust my memory.
Action: Search your notes and past chats from last spring for what you found, confirm the tulip festival and other kid-friendly event dates for the May long weekend, and send you a short list.

'ACH' is the US term (Automated Clearing House); in Canada the equivalent batch rail is usually called EFT, with direct deposit and pre-authorized debits as the common forms. So the person on the call was probably using ACH loosely to mean the Canadian EFT. The practical difference is mostly vocabulary, not a different product.
Action: I can write a one-line note on the terms you can paste into your own call notes.

I'm here, and living in a house full of drywall dust is a lot. For the floors: skip dry sweeping, since it pushes the fine dust around and any grit can scratch. Go over them with a vacuum on the hard-floor setting and a soft brush head, then a barely damp microfiber mop, rinsing the cloth often. Sam meant well.
Action: Nothing to book, I'll stay with you here if you want to keep talking.

Got it, I'll record that: no replacing the 2019 Mazda CX-5 in 2026, the money goes to the kitchen renovation, and you'll revisit an EV in 2028. I'll also get you off the dealer's lists.
Action: Find the dealer's emails, unsubscribe, set a filter to archive anything further from them, and save the car decision in a note.

Join as many waitlists as possible now and ask each about cancellations. Also look at licensed home child care agencies, which usually have openings sooner. Widen the area slightly to Parkdale or High Park.
Action: Pull a list of licensed centres and home child care agencies near Roncesvalles from the City of Toronto and send it to you.

I don't have the Ottawa flight search in front of me, so I'll dig it up instead of guessing prices. I'll also open your podcast note and base new picks on it.
Action: Find the earlier Ottawa flight comparison and send Sam the fares and times, then open your podcast note and send you a few new commute podcasts based on what you like.

I can do that once I know exactly which link to look for. I'd start with the beta materials, then your other docs, and list every one that still points to the old pricing page along with the new URL to swap in.
Action: Confirm the old pricing page URL from the marketing notice, search your docs for it, and send you a list of affected docs with the replacement link.

Here's a draft: 'Hi all, thanks for organizing the street party. I can take the 2 to 4pm slot at the lemonade table, but I won't be able to help with setup. Best, Riya'
Action: Save it as a draft for your OK before sending.

That's a lot to absorb in one week, and the Tuesday morning one is the one you protect, so being annoyed makes sense. I'll plan the Montreal day trip, but I need the bank meeting time from Tom before booking anything.
Action: Search morning flights and VIA trains Toronto to Montreal on Thu the 8th with a return early enough for dinner, add the options and prices, and check the meeting time with Tom before holding anything.

Here's the note: 'Heads down on focus time until 3:00. Ping me if it's urgent, otherwise I'll catch up after.'
Action: Set your Slack status to heads down until 3pm now, and post the note to #payouts-team once you OK it.

Sent to Hannah. I don't have the v1 scope handy, so I'll pull what's in Instant Payouts v1 from the PRD and rollout doc before writing so I don't promise anything that isn't in it. The blurb will be four to five lines, calm and concrete, and say 'merchants'.
Action: Pull the v1 scope from the PRD, draft the 4 to 5 line blurb for Olivia's sales deck, and show it to you for approval before it goes.

Jess should weigh: what the unit would net monthly after mortgage, condo fees, taxes, insurance and vacancy, against what selling would free up. Taxes matter a lot: renting it changes how a later sale is taxed, and she should ask an accountant about an election to keep principal residence treatment for a few years. Add in landlord workload, tenant rules in her province, her plans for the sale proceeds, and how she'd feel about a market dip.
Action: Put this into a short list you can forward to Jess.

I'll pull the backsplash and wall ideas from your 'kitchen reno' note and saved photos. The tile quote rev 2 is $3,140 and covers backsplash plus floor, so whatever you pick for the wall behind the stove and sink should fit that.
Action: Pull the inspiration from your kitchen reno note and photos, send you a shortlist for the wall behind the stove and sink, and once you decide I'll text Nate (never call) before Monday.

Here's a starter list: backpack, water bottle, lunch and snacks in a labelled bag, sunscreen, hat, closed-toe shoes, a spare change of clothes, rain jacket, and a towel if there's water play. I haven't seen the camp's own list, so I'd check theirs and merge it with mine. Labelling goes on every item, plus the bag and the water bottle.
Action: Find the Riverdale Farm camp info for the official list, merge it into a checklist note with a 'label this weekend' section, and send it to you.
